Commentary.Commentary: All in readiness for the chase to begin. The umpires are on the field and the fielding team has taken their positions on the ground.
... THE RUN CHASE ...

Right then, that was a very quick first innings in favor of the visitors. The conditions suit the pacers and New Zealand will hope to work on that to try and defend the total. Bangladesh have an easy task ahead of them and they will be high on morale after their bowling performance. Will the Kiwis show their dominance or will the Tiger emerge victorious as they chase down 99 runs? We will find out soon. Join us in a short while for the run chase.

Tanzim Hasan Sakib is in for a chat. He says that it has been a really pleasing effort and feels confident about chasing this total. Mentions that he is happy to contribute to the team. Adds that he was all over the place in the last game and had come with a mindset to bowl the right lines and lengths in this game. Shares that the wicket was helpful and he got a good amount of swing and extra bounce off the surface.

Bangladesh will be very ecstatic with their performance. Their bowlers used the conditions brilliantly and troubled the Kiwi batters right from the start. The pacers bowled on the perfect lines and lengths. Tanzid Hasan gave the first two breakthroughs and opened up the game for the rest of the bowlers to chip in as well. Shoriful Islam came in on the action and took his three wickets at crucial times dismissing the man in form, Will Young. Soumya Sarkar too wanted some of the action as he cleaned up three batters in quick intervals. The pacers were very effective on this surface and they will get all the credit for restricting a strong side to a very low total. The fielders were also very agile and quick to stop as many runs as they could which put further pressure on the opposition. Mustafizur Rahman finished things off with his first of the day and it was the pacers dominance over the batters as they scalped all the 10 wickets.

New Zealand had a good few overs but after that, it was just not their cup of tea to build partnerships. Rachin Ravindra was the first to depart. Henry Nicholls struggled out there and he too was dismissed after scoring only a single run. Tom Latham also failed to score big followed by Will Young who was their highest scorer in the innings. Mark Chapman and Tom Blundell too failed to build a partnership and were dismissed in quick succession. Josh Clarkson looked to be aggressive but he was dismissed after playing a bad shot followed by Adam Milne. Adithya Ashok played a few good shots out there in the middle and he might have gained some confidence from that but he too was sent back to the pavilion. They were wrapped up for a mere 98 runs and it is a very low score in this format of the game.

Safe to say it was a pretty one-sided first innings and it was not the way anyone expected it to be. The Tigers were preying on the Kiwis from the start and didn’t allow them to creep back into the game. Bangladesh has managed to restrict the hosts to a very low score of 98 runs.

Mustafizur Rahman ends with a wicket to his name and New Zealand have been bowled out for 98!

Hello and a very warm welcome folks. It is matchday and we are awaiting the third and final ODI between Bangladesh and New Zealand. The venue for this clash is the McLean Parl in Napier.
... MATCH DAY ...

It is time for the final ODI of the three-match series between New Zealand and Bangladesh. With the Kiwis holding an unassailable 2-0 lead in the series, the third ODI at McLean Park in Napier is essentially a dead rubber. That said, New Zealand will want to continue the momentum, whereas Bangladesh will look to avoid a whitewash and gain momentum ahead of the T20I series. After being inserted into bat in the second ODI, Bangladesh were off to a shaky start before Soumya Sarkar's 169 powered the visitors to a challenging total. In pursuit of 292, New Zealand's batting unit came to the fore with Will Young's 89 and 95 from Henry Nicholls' 95, which took them over the line comfortably. With the series in the bag now, New Zealand might want to test their bench strength and rest some of their players who will be featuring in the T20I series. Finn Allen has rejoined the squad, and he is likely to get a look in, as might right-arm pacer Ben Sears. Will Young has been on song in this series, and he has been well supported by Tom Latham and Henry Nicholls. William O'Rourke has been impressive in his debut series, as has the other debutant, Josh Clarkson. Adam Milne and Jacob Duffy have not done too badly either, while spin twins Ish Sodhi and Adithya Ashok have chipped in as well. On the other hand, Bangladesh have been let down big time by their experienced batting department. Soumya Sarkar stepped up in the last outing, but a no-show with the bat from Najmul Hossain Shanto, Litton Das, and Mushfiqur Rahim has been a big issue. If the tourists are to pull a win out of the bag, their batting will have to click collectively as a unit. Even though Shoriful Islam and Hasan Mahmud have been tidy in the two games, Mustafizur Rahman and Mehidy Hasan have looked off-colour, which has done the Asian side no favour. Can Bangladesh produce a spirited performance to avoid the clean sweep? Or will New Zealand go on to inflict a whitewash? We shall find out together.
